figures.caption: Fig. 10. Dynamic angles change with rotation rate. When cohesion is minimal—as in a dry system—the surface angle increases with increasing rotation rate. When cohesion is important, however, it is possible for the surface angle to decrease with increasing rotation rate—contrary to conventional wisdom.

figures.caption: Fig. 11. Dynamic angle difference as a function of Co. When the difference between the wet and dry dynamic angle is plotted vs. Co, a dramatic transition is seen to occur near Co ≈ 1—similar to the effect of Bo_g on the static heap angle. The dashed line represents the asymptotic value of the angle difference (i.e., the difference becomes zero as cohesion vanishes).
